r.정치 구도: The country split in two after the Houthi rebels from the north seized the capital, Sanaa, in 2014. The internationally recognized government uses Aden in the south as its temporary capital and since 2022 has been led by a Presidential Leadership Council that brings together various anti-Houthi factions. Yet the government side is itself divided between the UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council, which wants an independent south, and forces backed by Saudi Arabia. The council seized the east in late 2025 but was pushed back by a Saudi-backed counteroffensive in January 2026; it announced its dissolution, yet part of it carries on under a new name. Amid the infighting, the Houthis pushed south in autumn 2026 and came within roughly 100 km of Aden.

t.why: It sits on the Bab el-Mandeb strait linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, so every ship traveling between the Suez Canal and the Indian Ocean passes its coast. From November 2023 the Houthis attacked merchant ships, citing the war in Gaza, and many shipping lines rerouted around the southern tip of Africa, sharply raising freight costs and journey times. The United States and Israel responded with repeated airstrikes on the Houthis. With Iran backing the Houthis and Saudi Arabia and the UAE backing their opponents, the war also has the character of a proxy contest between regional powers. The UN counts Yemen among the world's worst humanitarian crises.
t.rel: At war since 2014. The Houthi rebels who control the north are backed by Iran and have fought a Saudi-led coalition. The Houthis have also attacked ships passing through the Red Sea.
t.korea: South Korea established relations with North Yemen in 1985 and with South Yemen in 1990, shortly before the two Yemens unified. KOGAS, SK Innovation and Hyundai Corporation hold stakes in the Yemen LNG project and began importing its liquefied natural gas in 2009, but the civil war halted production in 2015. In 2018 more than 500 Yemenis traveled via Malaysia and entered Jeju without visas to seek asylum, sparking a heated debate over taking in refugees. Since 2009 South Korea has kept its Cheonghae Unit in the Gulf of Aden to escort ships.
t.know: Shibam is packed with 16th-century mud-brick high-rises and is called the 'Manhattan of the desert'.
etext: It was already the poorest country in the Arab world before the civil war, and the fighting has shrunk the economy dramatically. More than half the population needs humanitarian assistance.
Oil and gas at a standstill

Oil and gas made up most of its exports, but the LNG plant has been idle since 2015. Crude exports also stopped after Houthi drone attacks on export terminals in 2022, costing the government most of its revenue.
Sanaa and Aden each have their own central bank, and the same rial notes are worth very different amounts depending on the region. In the south the rial has plunged and prices have soared.

Money sent home by Yemenis working in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states is a lifeline for many families. The word 'mocha' comes from the Yemeni port of Mocha, and the country still exports small amounts of fine coffee and honey.
